title: Policies can be set to `active` status without any approved workflow history — `PolicyEdit.handleSave()` and `PolicyDetailView` Activate button accept `status: 'active'` with no `workflow_history` gate; entire review cycle bypassable; violates ISO 27001:2022 Clause 5.2
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/policy-management/PolicyEdit.jsx`, `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/policy-management/PolicyDetailView.jsx`, `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/policy/controllers/policy.controller.js`
**Root Cause:** `PolicyEdit.handleSave()` and the Activate button in `PolicyDetailView` both accept `status: 'active'` without querying `workflow_history` for a completed approval event. No backend guard rejects the transition.
**Impact:** Any `policy.write` user can publish any policy without a review cycle. ISO 27001 Clause 5.2 requires approved policies; an auditor requesting approval evidence finds none for any policy in the system.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
In `policy.controller.js` `updatePolicy`: `if (body.status === 'active') { const approved = await PolicyWorkflowHistory.findOne({policyId: id, event: 'approved'}); if (!approved) return res.status(403).json({error: 'Policy must have an approved review before activation'}); }`. In `PolicyDetailView.jsx`, hide the Activate button unless `policy.workflowHistory?.some(h => h.event === 'approved')`.
fixEvidence: Fully re-architected around a real state machine, explicitly citing PM-001. Backend: `policy.validation.js:59-62` `updatePolicy` validator now rejects any `status` field in `PUT /policies/:policyId` outright ('status cannot be changed via this endpoint — use POST /policies/:id/transition'). `policy-version.service.js:45-60` (`createVersionedUpdate`) additionally strips `status` from `WORKFLOW_MANAGED_FIELDS` server-side as defence in depth, with an inline comment citing PM-001 by name. The only path to `active` is `POST /policies/:policyId/transition` (`policy.routes.js:136-141`), gated by `requirePermission('policy.approve')` and delegated entirely to `WorkflowTransitionService.transition()` (`workflowTransition.service.js`), which enforces a real state graph (`core/constants/featureWorkflows.js:21-35`): `draft→assigned→under_review→{active|needs_revision|rejected}` — `active` is reachable ONLY from `under_review`, never directly from `draft`. Frontend: `PolicyEdit.jsx:692,811` explicitly `delete payload.status` before every save, with comments citing PM-001/PM-022. Verified end-to-end: no code path exists that can set a policy's DB `status` field to `active` without first passing through `under_review` via a permission-gated transition call.

title: `approveOutcome` hardcoded to `'closed'` in `ReviewDetail` — reviewer approval transitions policy to end-of-life `closed` state, not `active`; all approved policies labelled closed; auditor cannot identify active policy set; violates Clause 7.5
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/policy-management/ReviewDetail.jsx`
**Root Cause:** `const [approveOutcome, setApproveOutcome] = useState('closed')` — initialized to `'closed'` with no UI control to change it. Every approval transitions the policy to end-of-life state.
**Impact:** Every policy completing the review workflow ends up `closed` (end-of-life) instead of `active`. Auditors cannot find any active policies. All reviewer effort produces the wrong lifecycle outcome on every use.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Change `useState('closed')` to `useState('active')` in `ReviewDetail.jsx`. Optionally expose a select for `['active', 'active_pending_changes']` for cases where minor revisions are required before final activation.
fixEvidence: `ReviewDetail.jsx:143` now reads `const [approveOutcome, setApproveOutcome] = useState('active'); // always 'active' — approval moves policy to active state`. The submit handler (`handleSubmitReview`) no longer writes a raw status field at all — it POSTs `POST /policies/:policyId/transition` with an explicit `stateMap = { approve: 'active', reject: 'rejected', requestChanges: 'needs_revision' }` (`ReviewDetail.jsx:433-437`), which is validated and applied by the backend `WorkflowTransitionService` (see PM-001). An approval can now only ever resolve to the `active` state, never `closed`.

title: Required review checklist items not validated before approval — `handleSubmitAction` submits approval with all 4 required items unchecked; checklist is presentational only; violates ISO 27001:2022 Clause 7.5
statusRaw: 🔴 OPEN (flipped back from in_progress — frontend-only, no backend defense-in-depth)
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/policy-management/ReviewDetail.jsx`
**Root Cause:** `handleSubmitAction` does not validate `checklistItems` state before calling the approval API. All four required items can be unchecked and the approval still submits.
**Impact:** Review approval provides no assurance the policy meets quality standards. ISO 27001 Clause 7.5 audit evidence is invalidated — approved policies may be incomplete or non-compliant documents.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
In `ReviewDetail.jsx` `handleSubmitAction`, add before `setSubmitting(true)`: `const unchecked = REQUIRED_CHECKLIST_IDS.filter(id => !checkedItems.includes(id)); if (unchecked.length > 0) { setError(\`Complete all required checklist items before approving (\${unchecked.length} remaining)\`); return; }`.
fixEvidence:
`ReviewDetail.jsx:644-645` now derives `uncheckedRequired = checklist.filter(item => item.required && !item.checked)` (comment explicitly cites PM-003). `handleSubmitReview` (lines 352-365) blocks submission with a toast listing the outstanding items when `selectedAction === 'approve'` and `uncheckedRequired.length > 0`. This is structurally enforced, not just advisory: the Submit Review button itself is `isDisabled={selectedAction === 'approve' && uncheckedRequired.length > 0}` (line 1478), and the modal shows an inline warning alert listing exactly which required items remain (lines 1403-1418). RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-27, DOWNGRADED FROM fixed TO in_progress: this enforcement is frontend-only. Repo-wide grep for 'checklist' across `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/policy/` and `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/workflow/` returns zero matches. `policy.validation.js`'s `exports.transition` validator (the schema for `POST /policies/:policyId/transition`, the only endpoint that can move a policy to `active`) accepts only `targetState`/`notes`/`assignedTo`/`deadline` — no checklist field exists in the request contract at all, and `workflowTransition.service.js` performs no checklist-completeness check anywhere before applying `under_review → active`. Exactly like the PM-001/PM-022 lesson already documented in this agent's own Architecture note ('a permission-gated dropdown alone doesn't stop a raw API call'), any `policy.approve`-holding user (or a script/Postman call) can call `POST /policies/:policyId/transition` with `{targetState:'active'}` directly and skip the checklist entirely — the React component's disabled button and toast are the only gate. Severity kept at Critical (not downgraded) because the underlying ISO 27001 Clause 7.5 assurance gap — 'was this review adequate and complete' — is not actually closed, only made harder to trigger accidentally through the normal UI.
**Re-verified 2026-08-30** after pulling latest `vibrantix-backend`/`vibrantix-client-panel` (`feature/dev`): confirmed via `git diff --stat` that no `policy` or `workflow` module files were touched by this pull — status and analysis above are unchanged and re-confirmed directly against the current code (backend HEAD now 8641818, client-panel HEAD now d400be5a).
**Status flipped 2026-08-30:** the backend bypass has now been confirmed absent across three consecutive re-verifications with zero code movement toward closing it; `in_progress` implied active remediation that isn't happening. Flipped back to `open` — the assurance gap (a direct API/script call skips the checklist entirely) remains fully exploitable.

title: XSS via `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` without DOMPurify — `PolicyDetailView.jsx` line 738 renders `policy.content` as raw HTML with no sanitization; malicious scripts execute for all viewers; OWASP A03:2021
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/policy-management/PolicyDetailView.jsx`
**Root Cause:** Policy content rendered as raw HTML: `<div dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: policy.content }} />` with no sanitization. Any user with `policy.write` access can embed executable JavaScript visible to all readers.
**Impact:** Stored XSS (OWASP A03:2021). Malicious scripts execute in all viewers' browsers including executives and external auditors. During an ISO Stage 2 audit conducted on-screen, the auditor's browser session is at risk.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
`npm install dompurify`. In `PolicyDetailView.jsx`: `import DOMPurify from 'dompurify';`. Change render to: `<div dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: DOMPurify.sanitize(policy.content, { USE_PROFILES: { html: true } }) }} />`.
fixEvidence: Verified every `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` call site across the entire `policy-management/` component tree now routes through `DOMPurify.sanitize()`: `PolicyDetailView.jsx:151,1718` (`DOMPurify.sanitize(html, { USE_PROFILES: { html: true } })`), `PolicyDetailsDrawer.jsx:161,1076`, `PolicyEdit.jsx:165,1694` (sanitized inside the shared `markdownToHtml()` helper), and `ReviewDetail.jsx:5,949` (`DOMPurify.sanitize(policy.content || '')`). No remaining raw/unsanitized `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` usage found anywhere in `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/policy-management/`.

title: Coverage-percentage math in /policy-management never checks the mapped policy's lifecycle status - draft/archived/rejected policies count identically to active ones
description:
`policy.service.js::getComplianceScore` (lines 295-323) and `getComplianceGaps` (lines 365-377) fetch `Policy.findOne({policyId,isLatest:true}).select('version')` only to read `.version` - `policy.status` is never read or filtered on. `policy.repository.js::frameworkMappingStats` (lines 603-609, the query behind FrameworkMapping.jsx) filters only `PolicyControlMapping.status:'active'`, with its own comment admitting 'PolicyControlMapping soft-delete flag, not policy status' - no join back to Policy.status exists anywhere in the function. The org dashboard `frameworkCoverage` aggregate (lines 502-551) has the same gap. This directly contradicts the UI's own documented methodology: `PolicyComplianceDashboard.jsx:233-237`'s tooltip states the score is 'Percentage of active framework controls covered by at least one active policy' - false for the actual computation.

Because `setRequirementMappings`/`createControlMapping` have no status gate either, a policy can acquire framework/control mappings while still draft (this is exactly what the AI-Reader 'Adopt Policy & Triage Gaps' flow does in one step). That draft policy's mappings are then counted at full weight in the org-wide 'Avg Coverage %' stat, the per-framework coverage bars, and the individual policy's own compliance score.

Auditor-facing breakage: an auditor sampling the dashboard's '73% covered' claim, or a specific policy's compliance score, is looking at a number partly built from documents that have never been approved - not limited to AI-generated policies, any draft policy of any origin inflates the number the same way.
requirement: ISO 27001:2022 Clause 5.2 policy must be reviewed and approved; ISO/IEC 27007:2019 §6.3.2 evidence verifiability
